newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Moscow posts ousted Chechen leader to Africa.
newsitem.headline: Moscow posts ousted Chechen leader to Africa.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin on Friday named the ousted pro-Moscow leader of the breakaway republic of Chechnya as Russia's ambassador to Tanzania.
Doku Zavgayev, Chechnya's Soviet communist boss until forced out by secessionist rebels in 1991, won a flawed presidential election in December 1995 while Russian troops held the capital Grozny.

But Zavgayev, branded Moscow's "puppet" by the separatists, was chased from the mainly Moslem region once again last August when rebel guerrillas stormed the city and succeeded in forcing Yeltsin to withdraw all his forces.
Separatist commander Aslan Maskhadov was elected Chechen president in January after elections judged free and fair by international observers.
A month earlier, Maskhadov pledged to punish Zavgayev.
